name: Zelophehad
title: The Man Without Sons
summary: Zelophehad was a man from the tribe of Manasseh who died in the wilderness without leaving any sons. His five daughters brought their case to Moses and were granted permission to inherit their father's land allotment, leading to an important change in Israelite law regarding women's inheritance rights.

keyEvents.title: Zelophehad's Death in the Wilderness
keyEvents.description: Selophehad died in the wilderness during Israel's journey. He was not among those who rebelled with Korah's group, but died because of his own sin.

keyEvents.title: Selophehad's Daughters Present Their Case
keyEvents.description: The five daughters of Selophehad—Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah—stood before Moses, the priest Eleazar, and the leaders at the entrance to the tent of meeting, demanding to receive their father's inheritance.

keyEvents.title: The Lord Upholds the Daughters
keyEvents.description: The Lord told Moses that Selophehad's daughters were right and that they should receive an inheritance among their father's brothers. Their father's inheritance was to be transferred to them.

keyEvents.title: A New Inheritance Law in Israel
keyEvents.description: Through the case of Selophehad's daughters, a new law regarding inheritance was established: If a man dies without sons, his inheritance shall go to his daughters, and further to other relatives if there are no daughters.

keyEvents.title: Condition Regarding Marriage Within the Tribe
keyEvents.description: The leaders of the clan of Manasseh raised the concern that the inheritance might leave the tribe if the daughters married outside it. Moses ruled that Selophehad's daughters must marry within their father's tribe to retain the inheritance.

keyEvents.title: Selophehad's Daughters Marry Within the Tribe
keyEvents.description: Selophehad's daughters followed the Lord's command and married men from the clan of Manasseh, so that the inheritance remained within the tribe.
